This document uses data coming from the following article:

- Y. Xu,M.B. Harms,C.S. Green,R.C. Wilson, & S.D. Pollak,  Childhood unpredictability and the development of exploration, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 120 (49) e2303869120, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2303869120 (2023).

We aim to replicate some of the figures and analysis from the paper in order to get some insights for a new project (e.g. required sample size, amount of trials)

```{r}
# Study 2

# t-test
hr_study1 <- hr_wide_study1 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Primary")
hr_study2 <- hr_wide_study2 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Replication")
hr <- rbind(hr_study1,hr_study2)

a <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "directed_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
b <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "strategic_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
c <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "rt_5thchoice", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
d <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "reward_maximization", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
e <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "mean_reward", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c, d, e) %>% 
  flextable::flextable()

```



```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom) # Para extraer los coeficientes de los modelos ordenadamente

# 1. Definir la función para extraer los parámetros
get_exploration_params <- function(df) {
  
  # Ajustar el modelo logístico prediciendo la elección de alta información
  # en función de la diferencia de recompensa
  modelo <- glm(chose_high_info_value ~ reward_differential, 
                family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
                data = df)
  
  # Extraer los coeficientes
  coefs <- coef(modelo)
  beta_0 <- coefs["(Intercept)"]
  beta_1 <- coefs["reward_differential"]
  
  # Mapear los coeficientes a los parámetros cognitivos
  # (Se usa el valor absoluto para sigma porque el ruido siempre es positivo)
  sigma <- abs(1 / beta_1)      # Ruido de decisión (Exploración Aleatoria)
  A     <- beta_0 / beta_1      # Bono de Información (Exploración Dirigida)
  
  # Retornar como un data frame de una sola fila
  tibble(
    directed_exploration = A,
    random_exploration = sigma
  )
}

# 2. Aplicar la función a tu tabla por participante y por horizonte
# Nota: Filtramos NAs porque en la condición de información igual [2 2], 
# "chose_high_info_value" no debería estar definido.
parametros_cognitivos <- hr_long_study1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(chose_high_info_value), !is.na(reward_differential)) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
  # group_by(id, horizon) %>%
  group_modify(~ get_exploration_params(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. (Opcional) Pivotar la tabla si necesitas tener los horizontes en columnas 
# separadas para hacer las restas (ej. directed_exploration_H6 - H1)
parametros_anchos <- parametros_cognitivos %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = horizon,
    values_from = c(directed_exploration, random_exploration)
  )

# Ver el resultado
parametros_cognitivos %>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")

hr_wide_study1 %>% 
       select(id, directed_exploration)%>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")

hist(hr_wide_study1$directed_exploration)

```

YA TENGO EXPLORACIÓN DIRECTA Y ESTRATEGICA. AHORA CALCULAR RELIABILITY





```{r}


# 1. Function to calculate split-half reliability for a given dataset
calc_split_half <- function(data, metric_col) {
  # Assign random halves to each subject's trials (assuming 'game' is your trial unit)
  data_split <- data %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    mutate(
      rand_order = sample(row_number()),
      half = if_else(rand_order %% 2 == 0, "half_1", "half_2")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculate the score for each subject per half
  # Replace 'mean(score)' with your specific Horizon metric calculation
  scores <- data_split %>%
    group_by(id, half) %>%
    summarize(
      score = mean(.data[[metric_col]], na.rm = TRUE), 
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = half, values_from = score)
  
  # Calculate Pearson correlation and apply Spearman-Brown correction
  r <- cor(scores$half_1, scores$half_2, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  r_sb <- (2 * r) / (1 + r)
  
  return(r_sb)
}


calc_split_half(    data = df[df$game_length == 10,] , "chose_high_info_value")



```


```{r}

# 2. Function to downsample data and run permutations
evaluate_trial_counts_split_cor <- function(data, metric_col, trial_counts, permutations = 50) {
  
  # Create a grid of parameters to iterate over
  grid <- expand_grid(
    n_trials = trial_counts,
    perm = 1:permutations
  )
  
  # Map over the grid
  results <- grid %>%
    mutate(
      reliability = map_dbl(n_trials, function(n) {
        
        # Downsample data to 'n' trials per subject
        downsampled_data <- data %>%
          group_by(id) %>%
          slice_sample(n = n, replace = FALSE) %>%
          ungroup()
        
        # Calculate reliability for this subset
        calc_split_half(downsampled_data, metric_col)
      })
    )
  
  # Summarize the results across permutations
  summary_results <- results %>%
    group_by(n_trials) %>%
    summarize(
      mean_reliability = mean(reliability, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_reliability = sd(reliability, na.rm = TRUE),
      ci_lower = quantile(reliability, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
      ci_upper = quantile(reliability, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  return(summary_results)
}


```





```{r}

# 1. Function to calculate ICC for a given downsampled dataset
calc_icc <- function(data, metric_col) {
  # Prepare data: subjects as rows, trial numbers as columns
  # Note: requires a 'trial_number' column to track items
  wide_data <- data %>%
    select(id, {{metric_col}}) %>%
    mutate(trial_number = 1:n(), .by = "id") %>% 
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = trial_number, 
      values_from = {{metric_col}},
      values_fn = mean # In case of duplicate trial numbers in a subset
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("id")
  
  # Calculate ICC using the psych package
  # The 'ICC3k' model matches the mean-rating consistency model used in the paper
  icc_res <<- psych::ICC(wide_data, missing = FALSE)
  
  # Extract just the ICC3k value
  # return(icc_res$results["ICC3k", "ICC"])
  return(icc_res$results["Average_fixed_raters", "ICC"])
}

calc_icc(df[df$horizon_f == "short",], "chose_high_info_value")

# 2. Function to downsample data and run permutations
evaluate_trial_counts_ICC <- function(data, metric_col, trial_counts, permutations = 50) {
  
  # Create a grid of parameters to iterate over
  grid <- expand_grid(
    n_trials = trial_counts,
    perm = 1:permutations
  )
  
  # Map over the grid
  results <- grid %>%
    mutate(
      reliability = map_dbl(n_trials, function(n) {
        
        # Downsample data to 'n' trials per subject
        downsampled_data <- data %>%
          group_by(id) %>%
          slice_sample(n = n, replace = FALSE) %>%
          ungroup()
        
        # Calculate reliability for this subset
        calc_icc(downsampled_data, metric_col)
      })
    )
  
  # Summarize the results across permutations
  summary_results <- results %>%
    group_by(n_trials) %>%
    summarize(
      mean_reliability = mean(reliability, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_reliability = sd(reliability, na.rm = TRUE),
      ci_lower = quantile(reliability, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
      ci_upper = quantile(reliability, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  return(summary_results)
}
```

```{r}


# Define the trial counts you want to test (e.g., from 20 up to 100 in steps of 10)
trial_levels <- seq(10, 80, by = 10)

# Run the simulation (using 100 permutations for stability)
set.seed(42) # For reproducibility
reliability_curve <- evaluate_trial_counts(
    data = df, 
  metric_col = "chose_high_info_value", 
  trial_counts = trial_levels, 
  permutations = 100
)

reliability_curve = reliability_curve %>% 
  mutate(method = "Spearman-Brown")

# Plot the results
ggplot(reliability_curve, aes(x = n_trials, y = mean_reliability)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.7, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") + # 0.7 is a common acceptable threshold
  labs(
    title = "Reliability of Horizon Task by Trial Count",
    x = "Number of Trials (Games) per Subject",
    y = "Spearman-Brown Corrected Reliability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r}
# Prepare full dataset with factor-coded horizon
df_full <- df %>%
  filter(horizon %in% c(1, 10)) %>% # Adjust levels if using 1 vs 5/6
  mutate(horizon_factor = factor(horizon, levels = c(1, 10), labels = c("H1", "H10")))

# Model formula with interaction
full_model_formula <- chose_high_info_value ~ horizon_factor * reward_differential

# Run simulation for the Horizon Effect
set.seed(42)
horizon_effect_reliability <- evaluate_param_reliability(
  data = df_full,
  formula = full_model_formula,
  target_coef = "horizon_factorH10",
  trial_counts = seq(20, 60, by = 10),
  permutations = 100
)
```
